module_role: Register-level + queue-pair host-controller interface for non-volatile storage attached over PCI Express (NVMe over PCIe) or a fabric transport (NVMe over Fabrics). NVMe defines (a) the controller register set in BAR0/BAR1, (b) the 64-byte command + 16-byte completion format, (c) the Submission/Completion Queue ring semantics, (d) the Admin Command Set + NVM I/O Command Set, (e) PRP/SGL data buffer descriptors, (f) interrupt mechanisms (MSI/MSI-X/INTx), (g) namespaces + virtualization (SR-IOV) + multi-path I/O.

integration_overview.transport: PCI Express (Base 1.4 binding). The NVMe controller is a PCI Function — single Function, multi-Function, or SR-IOV PF+VF.
integration_overview.register_region_size: ≥ 4 KB BAR0/BAR1 for the standard register set (offsets 0h..14h plus doorbells at 1000h+).
integration_overview.interrupts: MSI-X preferred; controller advertises MSI-X table in its PCIe MSI-X Capability. Falls back to MSI (single / multi message) or pin INTx for legacy hosts.
integration_overview.namespaces: Each namespace is a quantity of non-volatile storage formatted into logical blocks; referenced by 32-bit Namespace ID (NSID).
integration_overview.private_vs_shared: Private namespaces are attached to one controller; shared namespaces are attached to multiple controllers (multi-path / namespace sharing).
integration_overview.queue_ownership: Each I/O Queue belongs to one controller; SQ-to-CQ mapping is 1:1 or n:1 (multiple SQs can share one CQ).
integration_overview.memory_buffers_optional: Controller Memory Buffer (CMB) and Persistent Memory Region (PMR) optionally expose controller-local memory mapped into host address space.

interface_categories: PCI Express link (PCIe PHY + DLL + TL)
PCI Configuration Space (Type 0 header + Capability Structures: PCI Express Cap, MSI/MSI-X Cap, AER, Power Mgmt, Vendor Specific)
BAR0/BAR1 MMIO register region (CAP, VS, INTMS/INTMC, CC, CSTS, NSSR, AQA, ASQ, ACQ, CMB/PMR/BP regs, doorbells)
Host system memory (SQ/CQ rings + PRP lists + SGL segments + data buffers + metadata buffers)
Non-volatile storage media interface (NAND / NOR / 3D-XPoint / SCM / RAM-backed; vendor-internal)
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single PCI Function, single NVMe Controller, single port (M.2 / U.2 / AIC SSD)
Multi-Function PCI device — multiple NVMe Controllers sharing PCIe port (Figure 4 of Section 1.4)
Multi-port NVMe subsystem — multiple PCIe ports each with its own controller, sharing namespaces (Figure 5)
SR-IOV — single Physical Function + multiple Virtual Functions, each presenting an NVMe Controller (Figure 6)
NVMe-oF — same protocol shape rebound to RDMA / TCP / Fibre Channel (separate spec)
default_signal_values_when_omitted: PCIe link defaults from PCI Express Base Spec; NVMe controller registers default to 0 after PCIe Conventional Reset except read-only HwInit fields (CSTS.CFS, CSTS.NSSRO) which initialize per controller bring-up; CC = 0; CC.EN = 0; CSTS.RDY = 0; CSTS.SHST = 00b.
soc_dependent_items: Host SoC PCIe Root Complex / Root Port (NVMe host side)
Host IOMMU (Intel VT-d / AMD-Vi) for SR-IOV and DMA remapping
Host DRAM controller — backs SQ/CQ rings + data buffers + IOMMU page tables
Host MSI-X delivery: APIC / LPI in ARM GIC
On the device side: PCIe PHY + Controller IP + NAND/SCM media controller + DRAM cache + Power-Loss Protection (PLP) capacitors
Form factor: M.2 (2230/2242/2280/22110), U.2 (SFF-8639), AIC (PCIe slot), EDSFF E1.S / E1.L / E3.S / E3.L

pcie_capabilities_required.name: PCI Express Capability
pcie_capabilities_required.purpose: Reports endpoint capabilities, link width/speed, Device Control 2 (ARI / Extended Tags / etc.)

pcie_capabilities_required.name: MSI or MSI-X Capability
pcie_capabilities_required.purpose: Interrupt delivery; MSI-X strongly preferred (per-vector mask)

pcie_capabilities_required.name: Power Management Capability
pcie_capabilities_required.purpose: D0..D3hot states; D3cold for full power off

pcie_capabilities_required.name: SR-IOV Capability
pcie_capabilities_required.purpose: Required for SR-IOV multi-VF NVMe deployments

pcie_capabilities_required.name: Class Code 010802h
pcie_capabilities_required.purpose: PCI Base Class 01h (Mass Storage), Subclass 08h (NVMe), Programming Interface 02h (NVM Express)

low_power_modes.PS0..PSx: NVMe Power States (advertised in Identify Controller PSD array) — controller-managed power/performance trade-off (Section 8.4).
low_power_modes.Autonomous Power State Transition (APST): Set Features FID 0Ch — controller autonomously transitions to lower power state after idle window.
low_power_modes.D0..D3hot: PCI Express Power Management D-states; D3hot retains PCI configuration; D3cold loses everything.
low_power_modes.Host Memory Buffer (HMB): Set Features FID 0Dh — controller borrows host DRAM as cache; freed on D3cold.

compatibility_notes: An NVMe 1.4 controller may advertise older VS values (1.0/1.1/1.2/1.3) if it only implements that feature subset; OSes are expected to gracefully handle mixed-version controllers.
PCIe class code 010802h identifies the controller as NVMe; OS loads its NVMe driver based on class code, not vendor/device ID.
CC.IOSQES=6 (64 B) and CC.IOCQES=4 (16 B) are the only values supported for the NVM Command Set in 1.4; future I/O Command Sets in NVMe 2.x may use different sizes.
NVMe-oF rebinds the same protocol on RDMA/TCP/FC; the same Identify Controller / Identify Namespace structures are used over the fabric.
Boot Partitions (CAP.BPS=1) allow UEFI-less boot of small platforms via BPINFO/BPRSEL/BPMBL register sequence.
